name: doc-publish-google
description: Publish a Curia document (OKF workspace path) as a formatted Google Doc: headings, lists, bold, links and tables render as rich text, never as Markdown syntax. The document's Markdown goes to Google directly, so you never retype it. The first publish creates the Doc in Curia's Drive and records it in the document's `google_doc` frontmatter. Publishing again updates that same Doc from the current document. That replaces the Doc's whole content, so it is refused when someone edited the Doc or left open comments since the last publish; the refusal says what to do. The new Doc is not shared with anyone.

inputs.title: string? (the Doc's title. Defaults to the document's frontmatter title, then its file name. On a later publish, renames the Doc.)
inputs.folder_id: string? (Drive folder ID for a new Doc. Defaults to My Drive. Ignored when the document already has a Doc.)
inputs.overwrite: boolean? (replace the Doc even if it was edited or has open comments since the last publish. Default false.)

outputs.note: string? (anything the caller should know, e.g. the document changed while publishing)
